Ben —

Appreciate the detailed pack. Quick read-through notes before the sync: 

1) Outbound NAT: For private deployments we support two modes. For Anchorage I recommend customer-managed SNAT (egress through your NAT cluster) to keep telemetry IPs under your control; Redwood can fall back to our egress nodes if you need short-term burst capacity. Please confirm whether you require stable CIDR for our telemetry IPs — we can reserve a small block if needed.

2) KV-cache ports: 61000-62000 is fine from a firewall perspective, but we prefer TCP-only for stability. If you have UDP-based peer discovery, note that Redwood's runtime heartbeats are TCP.

3) Control/data separation: The PDF shows a shared management VLAN between control and data. For compliance we typically recommend an isolated control-plane VLAN with ACLs preventing tenant-data plane access except via the control service port (443/8443). Can you mark in the PDF which switches will carry the control VLAN?

I've pasted the relevant internal runbook link below — it lists our expectations for observability and telemetry certificates.

Thanks Karthik — attached is the annotated port map (anchorage_portmap_v2.csv) with control VLAN tags in the third column and an updated single-slide topology exported as PDF. A few clarifications inline below.

- Telemetry CIDR: We can allocate a /28 from our transit pool and reserve it for Redwood telemetry — please advise which IP range you prefer, or we can hand the /28 to you after cutover for your ingestion nodes.
- KV-cache: we'll switch to TCP-only for those ports; discovery stays on 61001.
- Firewall cluster: HA pair will terminate TLS and route to the control VLAN over VXLAN.

Attachment: anchorage_portmap_v2.csv (updated)
